$comment: Who owns each committed data file, in a form a program can read.
Prose said this in four places and none of them was checked, so a file
could be hand-edited, or written by a pipeline and never committed, and
nothing noticed. tests/test_generated_files.py holds this table to the
repository: every path here exists, every writer here exists, and every
committed data file is classified by it.
`staged_by_refresh` is the list scripts/refresh-daily.sh commits. It is
read from this file rather than retyped into a workflow, which is how
data/drought/usdm-huc4.json came to be recomputed every morning and
`appears_when` marks a path whose writer creates it only under a stated
condition, so it is owned and classified from the day the writer learns
to write it rather than from the day it first appears. Everything else
in this table still has to exist.

classes.generated-daily: Rewritten by the scheduled refresh. Never hand-edit; change the writer and run it.
classes.generated-weekly: Downloaded by the scheduled refresh when the producer publishes. Never hand-edit.
classes.generated-archive: Append-only history written by a generator. Never hand-edit, never rewrite in place.
classes.derived-on-demand: Rebuilt by a named tool when its inputs change, not by the daily job.
classes.reviewed-by-hand: Edited by a person, carrying the evidence for each entry.
classes.frozen: Retained for compatibility and parity checks. Do not regenerate.

files.note: The published reservoir payload. This commit is the deploy (ADR-002).
Verified exclusive polygons. Reverted rather than published alone when coverage fails.

The week usdm-current.geojson replaced, kept so a change between two weeks can be measured from the polygons rather than from basin shares. Rotated only when the map date actually moves. No page fetches it and the build does not publish it.
files.appears_when: the monitor publishes a week after the one held in usdm-current.geojson

files.note: The default level. Must describe the same week as the polygons.
The other offered level (ADR-064). A reader who changes the level fetches this file, so it is committed with the others or it strands them on another week.

The coarsest offered level (ADR-073). Committed with the other two for the same reason: a reader who changes the level fetches this file, and a week behind the others is a level that disagrees with itself.
The drought-only subbasin level (ADR-088). It is committed with the other coverage files but starts without an archive or previous-week claim.
One archive per level; merge_history refuses a payload at another. This is where the default level's previous week comes from.
The subregion archive (ADR-074). Started later than the basin one, so it holds fewer weeks and its level says so rather than pretending to a comparison it cannot make.
The region archive, on the same terms as the subregion one.
Derived from capacities, counties and the boundary files. tests/test_refresh.py runs the same --check comparison, so drift fails the build.
A median over a period that has ended cannot change. Network job; every run merges.
What drains to each published reservoir, traced once against NLDI and committed with its COMID evidence (ADR-077). Rebuild when the roster or snow network changes; published verbatim in dist.
A missing mask stops the drought run rather than reporting border basins as drought-free (ADR-059).
The drawn scope. Committed for reproducible analysis, never copied to dist/.
The ten-basin research scope. Registered, not published.
